sections.html:
Every Virginia eviction begins with a request to a magistrate, a court clerk, or a general district court judge for a summons. A sworn statement of the facts that justify removing the tenant goes with it. The case is called an unlawful detainer and is filed under Va. Code 8.01-126.

In a residential case the first hearing is meant to come as soon as practicable, and no later than 21 days after filing. When the docket cannot take it that fast, it still has to be heard within 30 days. The tenant must be served at least 10 days ahead of the return date. A landlord may request a later first date, and the court then picks one that suits both sides and the court.

Paperwork sets a floor. No order of possession can be entered unless the landlord has shown the tenant a proper termination notice and the court has accepted that notice into evidence. With no notice in the record, the judge has nothing to base possession on.

Owners thinking of selling a rented house should know that court calendars and notice periods decide how long the tenant stays, not the day you choose to list.

What the tenant did decides which notice applies, and each has its own clock under Va. Code 55.1-1245. These are the pieces that matter most when a rented house is headed for sale.

SituationWhat the landlord must do
Unpaid rentGive written notice, then wait 14 days for the tenant to pay before terminating and suing for possession
Breach that can be fixedGive notice that the lease ends no sooner than 30 days after receipt unless the problem is fixed within 21 days
Breach that cannot be fixedGive notice that the lease ends no sooner than 30 days after receipt
Criminal or willful act threatening health or safetyEnd the lease immediately and seek possession; first hearing within 15 calendar days of service
Repeat breach of the same kindGive a 30-day notice that refers to the earlier breach
Tenant who is a family abuse victimLease does not end solely because of abuse against the tenant, if the abuser is barred by the landlord or a court order

A fixable breach does not end the lease when the tenant fixes it before the date in the notice. On a rent default, that window is how a tenant who catches up keeps the home.

sections.h2: Landlords with more than four rentals
sections.html:
From July 1, 2027, a landlord with more than four rental units, or more than a 10 percent interest in more than four, must offer a payment plan before using the 14-day pay-or-quit route in certain small-balance cases. The Virginia legislature's text of 55.1-1245 shows the version for that date next to the current one.

  • It applies when the exact rent owed is no more than one month's rent plus contracted late charges.
  • The notice states the exact amount and offers equal monthly installments over the shorter of six months or the time left on the lease.
  • The tenant may pay off the balance early without penalty, and no extra late fees accrue while payments are on time.
  • The landlord has to make the offer only once during the rental agreement.
  • A tenant who neither pays nor enters the plan within 14 days can be terminated, and the landlord proceeds to court.

Owners of four or fewer units fall outside that subsection. With a single rented house you will usually serve the ordinary 14-day notice, but read your lease and ask a Virginia attorney which version applies on the day you serve it.

With a possession judgment in hand, the landlord requests a writ of eviction and the sheriff carries it out. Timing comes from two statutes, 8.01-129 and 8.01-471.

  • The tenant has 10 days from judgment to appeal to circuit court. The appeal bond and writ tax are due within those 10 days.
  • A defendant found indigent is excused from the appeal bond.
  • On request, the judge can order the writ to issue at once, but the sheriff cannot evict until the 10-day appeal period is over.
  • The sheriff serves notice of the eviction date and time at least 72 hours before executing the writ.
  • If the tenant perfects an appeal, the sheriff returns the writ to the clerk who issued it.

Issuance has to happen within 180 days of the judgment. After that the writ is returnable within 30 days, and one that goes unexecuted for that long is vacated by operation of law without another order. No writ can issue if landlord and tenant sign a new written rental agreement after the judgment.

sections.h2: What a landlord can collect besides possession
sections.html:
Under Va. Code 55.1-1251, ending the lease gives the landlord a claim for possession and rent. A separate claim covers actual damages, reasonable attorney fees, and the cost of serving notices and process.

Actual damages may include rent that would have fallen due until the term ends or a new tenancy starts, whichever comes first. The landlord must work to limit them, and a post-possession damages case cannot seek accelerated rent through the end of the term.

The court can award possession and a money judgment together, and the money judgment need not be reduced by the security deposit first. Once the tenant is gone, whether by choice or by writ, the deposit is credited under the deposit statute, which allows 45 days for an itemized statement.

These claims belong to the landlord. Whether a particular judgment stays with the seller or moves with the house depends on the contract, so have an attorney read it before closing.

sections.h2: Selling a rented house with an eviction pending
sections.html:
An open eviction does not block a sale. It does change what the buyer takes on. The closing transfers a deed, and the tenant's rights survive a change of owner.

  • Whoever holds the landlord's interest when the tenancy ends is bound by the security deposit statute and must return any deposit owed, even if it never changed hands with the property.
  • No unlawful detainer for a lease violation can be filed or kept going until the tenant has received the statement of tenant rights and responsibilities.
  • A hearing date, an appeal, or an unexecuted writ can push back the day the house is empty, so leave room in the closing date.

Cash Home Buyers talks with owners in every one of these positions, including houses with tenants in place. A conversation about the lease and any court papers is the quickest way to see what a sale would involve. We do not give legal advice, so take the eviction file to an attorney too.

sections.h2: Former owners after a foreclosure sale
sections.html:
A former owner still living in a single-family home on the day of the foreclosure sale is treated by Virginia as a tenant at sufferance. The new owner can end that tenancy by written notice given at least three days before the termination date, then file an unlawful detainer once the three days run out.

Fair rental value is owed from the foreclosure date until the person leaves, along with damages and reasonable attorney fees and court costs. The rule sits in 8.01-126, the same section that governs the eviction case.

Someone who rented from the foreclosed owner is a different case with different notice rules, described earlier on this page. If you cannot tell which category an occupant is in, ask the clerk of your local general district court before filing.

Each general district court keeps its own docket, filing hours, and fee schedule, and some localities attach local resource sheets to the summons. Call the clerk of the court where the rental house sits for current filing steps, fees, and hearing days.

faqs.q: How long does a Virginia eviction take from notice to lockout?
faqs.a: No single number fits. A 14-day rent notice, a first hearing 21 to 30 days after filing, a 10-day appeal window, and at least 72 hours of sheriff notice each add time, and an appeal adds more.

faqs.q: Can a landlord remove a tenant without a court order?
faqs.a: No. Only a sheriff executing a writ of eviction can remove a tenant, and the writ follows a possession judgment in an unlawful detainer case.

faqs.q: How long is a writ of eviction valid?
faqs.a: It must issue within 180 days of the judgment and is returnable within 30 days of issuance. If it is not executed in 30 days it is vacated automatically.

faqs.q: Can a tenant stop an eviction by paying?
faqs.a: Often, if done before the notice period ends. A rent notice allows 14 days to pay, and a fixable breach does not end the lease if fixed in time. After judgment, a new written rental agreement blocks the writ.

faqs.q: Who keeps the security deposit if the rental is sold?
faqs.a: Whoever holds the landlord's interest when the tenancy ends must return any deposit owed to the tenant, even if the deposit did not change hands at closing.
